title: The Tide of Sandpiper Point Again
premise: Marine biologist Sable Almeida has spent three years at Sandpiper Point counting sea turtles and avoiding her own heart after a betrayal that ended her engagement and her career in Boston. When Theo Marchetti — the stranger whose anonymous letters have anchored her through the darkest years — buys the cottage next door, she discovers he is also the man whose testimony once destroyed her mentor, the reason she fled to this coast in the first place. As turtle-nesting season peaks and the last ferry of autumn approaches, Sable and Theo must decide whether love can survive the truths they've both been hiding: hers about what really happened in Boston, his about why he wrote the letters at all. In the end, Sable chooses to stay past the last ferry, releasing a tagged turtle together with Theo and finally forgiving herself for a mistake that was never hers.
about_author: Bram Sterling is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who now writes coastal romances from a converted bait shop on the Atlantic seaboard. Their novels are known for salt-weathered settings, slow-burning second chances, and heroines who know more about the ocean than about their own hearts.

chapters.title: Nest Counts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Opening on a dawn turtle survey, we meet Sable's carefully measured life at Sandpiper Point: routine, research logs, and a locked box of ten years of unsigned letters. When a moving truck arrives at the neighboring cottage, she pretends not to care. Emotional beat: guarded contentment cracked by the first tremor of change.

chapters.title: The Man Next Door
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo unpacks boxes containing drafts of every letter he never signed, rehearsing a confession he's carried across a decade. He and Sable collide over a disputed property line and a stranded hatchling, sparking friction laced with recognition neither names. Emotional beat: longing disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: Letters in the Dune Grass
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A storm scatters pages from Theo's recycling bin; Sable reads handwriting identical to her anonymous correspondent's. She confronts him, and he admits only to 'writing letters once,' withholding the Boston connection. Emotional beat: hope arriving hand-in-hand with suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced to co-chair the town's nesting-season festival, Sable and Theo fall into easy rhythm — shared coffee, late-night nest watches, almost-kisses interrupted by duty. Meanwhile Sable's ex-fiancé emails: he's writing a memoir about Boston. Emotional beat: warmth deepening just as the past surfaces.

chapters.title: The Season's First False Crawl
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A mother turtle abandons her nest, mirroring Sable's own instinct to flee when Theo nearly kisses her and she pulls away, terrified of trusting again. She rereads the old letters and notices one dated the week of her mentor's disgrace — written by someone who knew too much. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Flashbacks reveal the truth: young researcher Theo testified against Sable's mentor in the data-fraud case, believing he was right, then learned the evidence was doctored by others. He began writing to Sable anonymously out of guilt. He burns his confession draft instead of giving it to her. Emotional beat: cowardice wrestling with conscience.

chapters.title: The Memoir Excerpt
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The ex-fiancé's published excerpt names 'T. Marchetti' as the star witness who ruined her mentor — and implies Sable falsified the data herself. Humiliated and convinced Theo befriended her out of pity or surveillance, she returns his festival partnership and bars him from the research station. Emotional beat: heartbreak weaponized by old shame.

chapters.title: Hatchling Rush
chapters.summary: Climax part one, alternating POV. A storm surge threatens hundreds of emerging hatchlings; despite their rupture, Sable and Theo work side by side through the night rescuing them. Soaked and exhausted, Theo finally tells her everything — the testimony, the forged evidence, the letters. Emotional beat: truth spoken in the dark, forgiveness still out of reach.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With the final ferry departing at dusk, Sable finds the letter Theo never sent — proof he'd spent years trying to undo the injustice, including evidence clearing her name entirely. She races the tide line to the dock, choosing between the safe mainland life she'd planned and the man who taught her the sea keeps no grudges. Emotional beat: the leap of faith.

chapters.title: What Stays
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. Spring returns to Sandpiper Point: Theo has helped reopen the inquiry into her mentor's case, Sable leads the station under her own name, and together they release the season's first tagged turtles. The locked letter box now sits open on their shared porch table. Emotional beat: belonging earned, identity reclaimed, love chosen over duty.
